WHO_2020_category: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (classic or solid variant); some mixed alveolar/embryonal
defining_lesion: t(2;13)(q35;q14) PAX3::FOXO1; ~55-60% of ARMS; frequent fusion-locus amplification; co-amplification of MYCN, CDK4, MIR17HG; low SNV burden
key_markers: Diffuse strong myogenin (MYOG) and MYOD1; desmin; AP-2beta (TFAP2B), P-cadherin, FGFR4, ALK; FOXO1 break-apart FISH positive
clinical_notes: Worst prognosis; fusion status now supersedes histology in COG/EpSSG risk stratification; metastatic FP-RMS 5-y EFS <20-30%; MYCN amplification and TP53 alteration further worsen outcome
pediatric_relevance: Older children and adolescents (median at the teenage end of the RMS age range)

defining_lesion: t(1;13)(p36;q14) PAX7::FOXO1; ~20-25% of ARMS; the fusion gene is nearly always genomically amplified
key_markers: Same myogenic markers as PAX3::FOXO1 (myogenin, MYOD1, desmin); FOXO1 break-apart FISH positive; distinct expression and DNA-methylation cluster from PAX3::FOXO1
clinical_notes: Better EFS/OS than PAX3::FOXO1 in both localized and metastatic disease, but still grouped as FP-RMS for therapy
pediatric_relevance: Younger than PAX3::FOXO1 cases (often <10 y); extremity primaries over-represented

subtype_name: Fusion-positive RMS with variant PAX3/PAX7 partners
WHO_2020_category: Alveolar or solid-variant RMS; rarely spindle cell
defining_lesion: PAX3::NCOA1 t(2;2)(q35;p23); PAX3::NCOA2; PAX3::INO80D; PAX3::MAML3; PAX3::FOXO4 (AFX); PAX7::NCOA1
key_markers: Myogenin/MYOD1/desmin positive; FOXO1 break-apart FISH is NEGATIVE - a major diagnostic pitfall; detection requires RNA-based fusion panel
clinical_notes: Rare (<2% of RMS); assumed to behave like FP-RMS but outcome data are very limited; PAX3::MAML3 cases are often sinonasal/head-and-neck
pediatric_relevance: Children and adolescents

WHO_2020_category: Solid-variant alveolar RMS; spindle cell RMS of bone
defining_lesion: FOXO1::FGFR1 (with amplification); MEIS1::FOXO1
key_markers: Myogenic markers positive; PAX3/PAX7 break-apart negative but FOXO1 break-apart positive
clinical_notes: Very rare; FOXO1::FGFR1 provides a rationale for FGFR-directed therapy
pediatric_relevance: Children and young adults

subtype_name: Congenital/infantile spindle cell RMS with NCOA2/VGLL2-family fusions
defining_lesion: VGLL2::NCOA2; VGLL2::CITED2; SRF::NCOA2; TEAD1::NCOA2; VGLL2::NCOA1
key_markers: Desmin positive, MYOD1 positive, myogenin usually patchy/weak; bland spindle-cell morphology; FOXO1 FISH negative
clinical_notes: Favourable: local recurrence occurs but metastasis and death are rare; good outcome, often with surgery alone
pediatric_relevance: Birth to approximately 1 year (congenital/infantile)

subtype_name: Spindle cell RMS with MEIS1::NCOA2 / ZFP64::NCOA2
defining_lesion: MEIS1::NCOA2; MEIS1::NCOA1; ZFP64::NCOA2; ZFP64::NCOA3
key_markers: Desmin positive; variable MYOD1/myogenin; low-grade spindle morphology; genitourinary/gynaecologic and intraosseous sites
clinical_notes: Frequently lower-grade behavior than MYOD1-mutant spindle RMS, but intraosseous cases can be aggressive; series are small
pediatric_relevance: Children through adults

WHO_2020_category: Spindle cell/epithelioid rhabdomyosarcoma, characteristically intraosseous (craniofacial bones)
defining_lesion: EWSR1::TFCP2 or FUS::TFCP2; frequent CDKN2A deletion; recurrent ALK overexpression/amplification and occasional ALK fusion (e.g. DCTN1::ALK)
key_markers: Co-expression of cytokeratin AE1/AE3 with myogenic markers (desmin, MYOD1, myogenin); ALK immunopositive - mimics metastatic carcinoma
clinical_notes: Highly aggressive with early metastasis and poor survival; poorly responsive to conventional RMS chemotherapy; ALK and CDK4/6 inhibition proposed
pediatric_relevance: Adolescents and young adults; female predominance reported

defining_lesion: MYOD1 p.Leu122Arg (c.365T>G) neomorphic MYC-like mutation, frequently homozygous via LOH; PIK3CA co-mutation in roughly one third of cases; also PTEN, AKT1, GNAS; TP53 alterations common
key_markers: Diffuse strong MYOD1 (often stronger and more diffuse than myogenin); desmin positive; sclerosing/hyalinized or fascicular spindle pattern; head-and-neck and deep extremity sites
clinical_notes: Highly aggressive irrespective of patient age or histologic pattern (spindle vs sclerosing); poor OS; managed as high risk; PIK3CA co-mutation gives a PI3K/AKT/mTOR targeting rationale
pediatric_relevance: Older children, adolescents and adults - occurs at any age

defining_lesion: No recurrent fusion detected in a subset; MYOD1 wild type; some cases carry as-yet unclassified NCOA2-family or other rearrangements
key_markers: Desmin positive, MYOD1 positive, myogenin patchy
clinical_notes: Generally favourable, comparable to fusion-positive infantile spindle cell RMS
pediatric_relevance: <1 year

defining_lesion: No PAX::FOXO1 fusion; LOH/uniparental disomy at 11p15.5 (IGF2 locus); whole-chromosome gains of 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13, 20; higher SNV burden than FP-RMS
key_markers: Patchy/variable myogenin, MYOD1 positive, desmin positive; FOXO1 FISH negative
clinical_notes: Better overall than FP-RMS; anaplasia and TP53 mutation confer markedly worse outcome; relapsed FN-RMS remains largely incurable
pediatric_relevance: Median <10 years; head/neck, genitourinary and orbital primaries

defining_lesion: NRAS (Q61), KRAS (G12/Q61) and HRAS (Q61) hotspot mutations; plus NF1 loss, PTPN11, BRAF; collectively ~40-50% of FN-RMS
key_markers: Myogenic markers as for FN-RMS; RAS-MAPK transcriptional signature
clinical_notes: Intermediate outcome within FN-RMS; MEK inhibition with or without IGF1R inhibition is under clinical investigation
pediatric_relevance: Infants and young children; HRAS mutations enriched in infants, including Costello syndrome-associated RMS

WHO_2020_category: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (FGFR4 is also a PAX3::FOXO1 target gene in FP-RMS)
defining_lesion: FGFR4 kinase-domain mutations (p.N535K, p.V550E, p.V550L); FGFR4 amplification/overexpression
key_markers: High FGFR4 protein expression; standard myogenic markers
clinical_notes: FGFR4 mutation associates with advanced stage and inferior survival; FGFR4 is an active CAR-T, ADC and TKI target
pediatric_relevance: Children

subtype_name: FN-RMS with TP53 mutation (somatic or germline / Li-Fraumeni)
defining_lesion: Somatic or germline TP53 mutation; anaplasia strongly enriched; frequent co-occurring MYCN or CDK4 amplification
key_markers: Anaplastic morphology; aberrant p53 immunostaining
clinical_notes: Independently associated with markedly inferior EFS and OS within FN-RMS; mandates germline testing and Li-Fraumeni surveillance
pediatric_relevance: Young children; germline TP53-associated RMS typically presents <3 years

subtype_name: FN-RMS with other recurrent drivers (FBXW7, BCOR, PIK3CA, CTNNB1, DICER1)
WHO_2020_category: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, including botryoid cervical/uterine ERMS
defining_lesion: FBXW7, BCOR, PIK3CA, CTNNB1, ARID1A mutations; DICER1 hotspot mutations in cervical/uterine botryoid ERMS
key_markers: Myogenic markers; DICER1-associated cases often show cartilaginous islands and arise in cervix/uterus
clinical_notes: Individually rare; DICER1-associated ERMS prompts germline DICER1 testing and pleuropulmonary-blastoma-tumor-predisposition surveillance
pediatric_relevance: Variable; DICER1-associated ERMS typically in adolescents and young women

defining_lesion: No recurrent fusion; highly complex genome with chromothripsis; near-universal TP53 loss/mutation and frequent RB1 loss
key_markers: Desmin positive, MYOD1 positive, myogenin often only focal; bizarre pleomorphic rhabdomyoblasts; deep extremity soft tissue
clinical_notes: Behaves as a high-grade adult pleomorphic sarcoma; poor prognosis; does not benefit from pediatric RMS chemotherapy regimens
pediatric_relevance: Adults, typically >40-50 years; very rare in children

WHO_2020_category: Ectomesenchymoma - biphasic rhabdomyosarcomatous plus neuroectodermal/ganglionic tumor
defining_lesion: Biphasic: an RMS component (usually embryonal, rarely alveolar or spindle) plus ganglioneuroma/ganglioneuroblastoma/neuroblastoma; molecularly overlaps FN-RMS with reported HRAS/RAS-pathway mutations; rare PAX3::FOXO1-positive cases; no single defining lesion established (unknown)
key_markers: Myogenin/MYOD1/desmin in the RMS component; synaptophysin, S100, PHOX2B, NB84 in the neural component
clinical_notes: Treated on RMS protocols; in the EpSSG series outcome is broadly comparable to stage-matched RMS; the neural component does not independently worsen prognosis
pediatric_relevance: Infants and young children (majority <5 years); head/neck, perineum and genitourinary sites

WHO_2020_category: Ewing sarcoma (Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas of bone and soft tissue)
defining_lesion: t(11;22)(q24;q12); EWSR1 ex7::FLI1 ex6
key_markers: CD99 strong diffuse membranous; NKX2-2 nuclear; FLI1 nuclear; PAX7; caveolin-1; ETV4 neg; WT1 neg
clinical_notes: ~60% of EWSR1::FLI1 cases; EWSR1::FLI1 = 70-85% of all EwS

defining_lesion: t(11;22)(q24;q12); EWSR1 ex7::FLI1 ex5
key_markers: same as type 1
clinical_notes: ~25% of EWSR1::FLI1 cases

subtype_name: Ewing sarcoma, EWSR1::FLI1 non-type1/2 (types 3, 4 and rare)
defining_lesion: EWSR1 ex7/9/10 :: FLI1 ex4/5/6/8 (e.g. type 3 = ex10/ex6; type 4 = ex10/ex5)
key_markers: same as type 1
clinical_notes: ~10-15% of EWSR1::FLI1 cases

key_markers: CD99; NKX2-2; ERG nuclear positive; FLI1 may be negative
clinical_notes: ~5-10% of EwS (EWSR1/FUS::ERG ~15% collectively)

key_markers: CD99; NKX2-2
clinical_notes: <1% (EWSR1::ETV1/ETV4 together ~1%)

key_markers: CD99; NKX2-2; ETV4 positive (overlaps CIC-rearranged sarcoma - do not use ETV4 alone)
CD99; NKX2-2
clinical_notes: <1-5% (EWSR1/FUS::FEV ~5% in consensus estimates)

key_markers: CD99; NKX2-2; ERG nuclear
CD99; NKX2-2
clinical_notes: <<1%; isolated case reports only

defining_lesion: EWSR1::FLI1 (most); rare FUS::FEV
key_markers: CD99 + AND pancytokeratin/p40/p63 positive (epithelial co-expression)
clinical_notes: rare; head/neck, thyroid, salivary gland

defining_lesion: STAG2 truncating mutation / deletion (Xq25)
key_markers: STAG2 IHC loss; largely mutually exclusive with CDKN2A deletion; amplifies GGAA-microsatellite enhancer activity and rewires enhancer-promoter contacts
clinical_notes: 15-22% of primary EwS; ~44% of EwS cell lines; 20% of PPTC EwS PDX

defining_lesion: TP53 missense/truncating
key_markers: p53 IHC aberrant; co-occurrence with STAG2 defines a highly aggressive subtype
clinical_notes: 6-10% of tumors; ~72% of cell lines (strong culture selection bias)

defining_lesion: homozygous 9p21.3 deletion
key_markers: p16 IHC loss; mutually exclusive with STAG2 mutation in PDX cohorts
clinical_notes: 12-22% of tumors; ~50% of cell lines; 60% of PPTC EwS PDX

WHO_2020_category: Ewing sarcoma (epigenetic mechanism, not a WHO entity)
defining_lesion: EWSR1::FLI1 binding to GGAA microsatellite repeats
key_markers: EWS-FLI1 prion-like/low-complexity domain recruits BAF(SWI/SNF); converts closed GGAA mSats into de novo H3K27ac/H3K4me1 enhancers; enhancer strength scales with repeat number; germline mSat length is a susceptibility modifier
clinical_notes: present in essentially all FET::ETS EwS

WHO_2020_category: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions
defining_lesion: t(20;22)(q13;q12); fusion is frequently amplified
key_markers: AGGRECAN positive; CD99 variable/dot-like; NKX2-2 negative; PAX7 positive; keratin/EMA may be positive; distinct DNA methylation class
clinical_notes: rare (<1% of round cell sarcomas); adults, male predominance, metaphysis of long bones

WHO_2020_category: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions
key_markers: similar immunoprofile; methylation profile distinct from EWSR1::NFATC2
clinical_notes: very rare

WHO_2020_category: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions
defining_lesion: intrachromosomal inv(22)(q12q12)
key_markers: polyphenotypic - co-expression of desmin/myogenin/MyoD1 with S100/SOX10/GFAP; PATZ1 IHC
clinical_notes: rare; thoracoabdominal predilection

key_markers: ETV4 positive; WT1 positive; DUX4 C-terminus nuclear positive; CD99 focal/patchy (not diffuse); NKX2-2 negative; calretinin positive
clinical_notes: ~2/3 of EWSR1-negative undifferentiated round cell sarcomas; ~95% of CIC-rearranged sarcomas

defining_lesion: t(10;19)(q26;q13); DUX4L paralogue on 10q26
key_markers: same as CIC::DUX4
clinical_notes: minority of CIC::DUX4-type fusions

defining_lesion: CIC::NUTM1
key_markers: NUT IHC positive; ETV4 variable; DUX4 negative
clinical_notes: rare variant (single-digit case series)

key_markers: ETV4 positive; DUX4 negative
clinical_notes: very rare

defining_lesion: CIC::LEUTX, CIC::NUTM2A
key_markers: ETV4 variable; DUX4 negative
clinical_notes: very rare

defining_lesion: ATXN1::DUX4 / ATXN1L::DUX4
key_markers: DUX4 positive; CIC FISH negative
clinical_notes: very rare; CNS

defining_lesion: inv(X)(p11.4p11.22) BCOR::CCNB3
key_markers: BCOR positive; CCNB3 nuclear positive; SATB2 positive; TLE1 positive; cyclin D1 diffuse positive; CD99 dot-like/variable
clinical_notes: ~60% of BCOR-altered sarcomas; ~4-5% of EWSR1-negative round cell sarcomas; marked male predominance, <20y, bone > soft tissue; 5y OS ~75%

defining_lesion: BCOR::MAML3
key_markers: BCOR overexpression
clinical_notes: rare

defining_lesion: ZC3H7B::BCOR (also in high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma)
key_markers: BCOR overexpression; cyclin D1
clinical_notes: rare

subtype_name: Undifferentiated round cell sarcoma with BCOR internal tandem duplication
defining_lesion: BCOR exon 15 internal tandem duplication
key_markers: BCOR positive; cyclin D1 positive; SATB2 positive
clinical_notes: infants (<1y); overlaps primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumor of infancy and clear cell sarcoma of kidney

subtype_name: Undifferentiated round cell sarcoma with YWHAE::NUTM2B/2A
WHO_2020_category: Sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations (related group)
defining_lesion: t(10;17) YWHAE::NUTM2B/NUTM2A
key_markers: BCOR positive; NTRK3 overexpression (not NTRK3 fusion)
clinical_notes: very rare

WHO_2020_category: Sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations (concept extension)
defining_lesion: KDM2B fusions (e.g. KDM2B::CXXC5)
key_markers: BCOR overexpression
clinical_notes: very rare

defining_lesion: High-grade intramedullary OS; predominant malignant osteoid/bone matrix (>50% osteoblastic)
key_markers: SATB2+, RUNX2+, SP7/Osterix+, ALPL+, COL1A1+

defining_lesion: High-grade intramedullary OS with predominant malignant hyaline cartilage matrix
key_markers: SOX9+, ACAN+, COL2A1+, S100+, SATB2+ in osteoid areas

defining_lesion: High-grade intramedullary OS with predominant spindle-cell/fibrous matrix and minimal osteoid
key_markers: SATB2+, vimentin+, low osteoid; MDM2/CDK4-negative

defining_lesion: Blood-filled cystic spaces with septa containing high-grade sarcoma cells; radiographically mimics aneurysmal bone cyst
key_markers: SATB2+; no USP6 rearrangement (distinguishes from ABC); frequent TP53 structural alteration

defining_lesion: Small round blue cells with lace-like osteoid; differential vs Ewing sarcoma
key_markers: SATB2+, CD99 variable/weak, EWSR1 FISH-negative, NKX2-2-negative

defining_lesion: Low-grade surface OS of the posterior distal femur metaphysis; parallel bony trabeculae in bland spindle stroma
key_markers: MDM2 and CDK4 amplification (12q13-15 supernumerary ring/giant marker chromosome); MDM2/CDK4 IHC+

defining_lesion: Intermediate-grade surface OS with predominantly chondroblastic differentiation, diaphyseal
key_markers: SOX9+; MDM2/CDK4 usually NOT amplified (distinguishes from parosteal)

defining_lesion: High-grade OS arising on the bone surface without medullary involvement
key_markers: SATB2+; genomics resembles conventional high-grade OS; MDM2-negative

defining_lesion: Low-grade intramedullary fibro-osseous lesion; mimics fibrous dysplasia/desmoplastic fibroma
key_markers: MDM2 and CDK4 amplification/overexpression; GNAS-negative

defining_lesion: High-grade OS arising in pagetic bone in older adults; poor prognosis
key_markers: Elevated ALP; SQSTM1/p62 germline variants in some Paget kindreds; complex karyotype

defining_lesion: High-grade OS arising in a prior radiation field, typically >3 y latency
key_markers: Complex genome; enriched in hereditary retinoblastoma and other irradiated childhood-cancer survivors

defining_lesion: ATAC-seq cluster enriched for RUNX2/RUNX3/MEOX2/MEF2 motifs; core regulatory circuitry RUNX2-SATB2-SP7-ZNF148; enriched for MYC-amplified PDX-derived lines; more aggressive in vivo; selectively sensitive to AURKB inhibition (AZD1152/barasertib)
key_markers: RUNX2-high, SATB2-high, SP7/Osterix-high, ZNF148-high, MEF2A/C/D, DLX2/DLX6, HOXA5, VAX2, c-MYC-high; RUNX2 is an EOD-selective DepMap dependency

defining_lesion: ATAC-seq cluster enriched for AP-1 motifs; core regulatory circuitry FOSL1-FOSL2-JUN-TEAD1-RUNX2; contains most long-term established OS cell lines; high p-ERK; selectively sensitive to MEK inhibition (trametinib)
key_markers: FOSL1-high, FOSL2-high, JUN/JUNB-high, TEAD1, NFATC2 (LOD-restricted CRC node), p-ERK-high, COL6A2/COL6A3 ECM DORCs; FOSL1 and JUN are LOD-selective DepMap dependencies

defining_lesion: Third cluster in hierarchical clustering of the 237-gene EOD/LOD signature in patient tumors; single-nucleus multiome shows EOD and LOD cells coexisting in one tumor plus an 'undetermined' fraction; EOD in biopsy shifting to LOD in resection/metastasis in 4 patients
key_markers: Co-expression of EOD (RUNX2/SP7/SATB2) and LOD (FOSL1/FOSL2/JUN) programs

defining_lesion: Third transcriptional subtype of osteosarcoma alongside the RUNX2-high and FOSL1-high subtypes, defined in a 60-patient Tel Aviv OS cohort profiled by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Subtype assignment is made by k-means quadrant gating on per-sample RNA-seq subtype scores, with the resulting groups corroborated by subtype-selective ATAC-seq peaks. NOT YET IN THE INDEXED LITERATURE: no PubMed, Europe PMC or AACR record describes a KLF1-defined osteosarcoma subtype, so it cannot currently be cited from a public source.
key_markers: KLF1-high (distinguishing it from the RUNX2-high and FOSL1-high subtypes); RNA-seq subtype-score quadrant assignment plus KLF1-subtype-selective ATAC-seq peaks
key_reference_PMID: unpublished (Chin et al., "RUNX2 is essential for active chromatin clusters in osteosarcoma and is vulnerable to p300 inhibition", Gryder lab, manuscript in preparation 2026)

defining_lesion: Low tumor purity, low proliferation, high immune infiltration; favorable prognosis
key_markers: BANK1-high, high immune/ESTIMATE score, low MYC and CCNE1 amplification

defining_lesion: Higher purity than S-IA, activated fatty-acid metabolism, immune exhaustion; intermediate-poor prognosis
key_markers: CD36 amplification, immune-exhaustion markers

defining_lesion: Highest tumor purity, extreme genomic instability, HRD-positive in 84.2%; relatively favorable with platinum
key_markers: TP53 and BRCA2 deletions, NSD1 loss, COSMIC signature 3 / BRCAness

defining_lesion: MYC amplification, OXPHOS activation, immune-cold; worst prognosis (5-y OS <40%) and chemoresistance
key_markers: MYC (8q24) amplification, OXPHOS signature

WHO_2020_category: immunogenomic (MD Anderson cohort n=48 + TARGET-OS validation)
defining_lesion: Lowest immune infiltrate, low TCR clonality, low neoantigen expression, high nonsense-mediated decay
key_markers: Low CD8A, low GZMA/PRF1 cytolytic score, low ESTIMATE/TIMER scores

defining_lesion: Relatively high immune infiltrate, enriched in older patients; upregulated immunosuppressive checkpoints
key_markers: CD8+ TIL-high, PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA4, IFNG pathway enrichment, high GZMA/PRF1

WHO_2020_category: transcriptomic ICA of TME (European/French cohort, n=79 discovery + 82 + 96 validation)
defining_lesion: Independent-component analysis of diagnostic biopsies; innate-immunity program; favorable overall survival
key_markers: Innate immune / myeloid signature; NanoString-validated focused gene signature

defining_lesion: Angiogenic, osteoclastic and adipogenic programs with PPARG pathway upregulation; poor overall survival
key_markers: PPARG pathway, angiogenesis, osteoclast and adipogenic signatures

WHO_2020_category: comparative transcriptomic (human n=49, mouse n=103, dog n=34)
defining_lesion: Conserved cross-species intertumor variation; gene cluster expression summary score (GCESS) for immune-cell content and for cell cycle/mitosis; low immune GCESS associates with metastasis and poor survival
key_markers: Immune-cell transcript cluster; cell-cycle/mitosis cluster

WHO_2020_category: single-cell transcriptomic (scRNA-seq, 7 primary + 2 recurrent + 2 lung met)
defining_lesion: Dominant malignant compartment in conventional OS
key_markers: COL1A1, CDH11, RUNX2

defining_lesion: Osteoblastic markers plus cycling program
key_markers: TOP2A, PCNA, MKI67 with COL1A1/RUNX2

defining_lesion: Cartilage-matrix program; trajectory analysis supports transdifferentiation of chondroblastic to osteoblastic malignant cells
key_markers: ACAN, COL2A1, SOX9

defining_lesion: Lower osteoclast infiltration in chondroblastic, recurrent and lung-metastatic lesions vs primary osteoblastic lesions
key_markers: CTSK, MMP9, ACP5

defining_lesion: 10 myeloid subclusters; pro-inflammatory FABP4+ macrophages enriched in lung metastases
key_markers: FABP4, CD68, CD163, C1QA

defining_lesion: NOT VERIFIED. No published osteosarcoma single-cell study using the specific state labels 'fibrogenic' or 'interactive' was found; the reproducible malignant-state labels are osteoblastic, proliferating/proliferative, chondroblastic, plus CAF and TAM compartments

Most frequent OS predisposition gene; ~28% of OS patients carry pathogenic/likely-pathogenic germline variants in cancer-susceptibility genes overall, TP53 most common; rare/low-frequency TP53 variants enriched in OS
key_markers: Germline TP53 missense/truncating and copy-number variants; somatic TP53 near-universally disrupted in sporadic OS

subtype_name: TP53 germline variants and OS susceptibility
defining_lesion: 9.5% of 765 OS cases carried rare exonic TP53 variants; 3.8% known LFS-associated
key_markers: Germline TP53

defining_lesion: Germline RB1 carriers have markedly elevated OS risk, further increased by radiotherapy; OS is the most common second sarcoma
key_markers: Germline RB1; somatic RB1 loss in ~30-40% of sporadic OS

defining_lesion: Biallelic deleterious RECQL4 variants; ~30% of RTS patients develop OS, often multifocal and at younger age
key_markers: Germline RECQL4 truncating variants; poikiloderma, skeletal dysplasia

defining_lesion: Adult progeria; OS is over-represented among Werner-associated neoplasms (soft-tissue sarcoma, OS, thyroid, melanoma, meningioma)
key_markers: Germline WRN (RECQL2) biallelic loss

defining_lesion: Biallelic BLM (RECQL3) loss; sister-chromatid exchange; broad early-onset cancer spectrum that includes osteosarcoma
key_markers: Germline BLM; elevated SCE on cytogenetics

defining_lesion: Markedly elevated overall cancer risk; solid tumors including reported osteosarcoma; OS is a rare but described DC malignancy
key_markers: Germline DKC1 (X-linked) and other telomere-maintenance genes; very short lymphocyte telomeres

subtype_name: Broad germline predisposition panel in osteosarcoma
defining_lesion: 28% of 1244 OS patients had P/LP variants in 1 of 238 cancer-susceptibility genes; enriched genes included TP53, CDKN2A, RECQL4, BRCA2, ATM, PTEN, RET
key_markers: Multigene germline panel

defining_lesion: Single catastrophic shattering-and-religation event; reported in 20-89% of OS and in the majority of PPTC OS PDX models; generates amplified oncogenic drivers
key_markers: Clustered rearrangements with oscillating copy number (2-3 states) on one or few chromosomes; frequently chr8, chr17

defining_lesion: Localized hypermutation clusters (C>T/C>G at TpCpN) co-localizing with rearrangement breakpoints; reported in 50-85% of OS
key_markers: APOBEC-type mutation clusters near SV breakpoints

defining_lesion: Recurrent focal 8q24 gain/amplification; defines the MYC-driven multi-omics subtype (S-MD), enriched in the EOD/RUNX2-high epigenetic subtype, associated with chemoresistance and CDK-inhibitor sensitivity
key_markers: MYC copy number >4; c-MYC protein high

defining_lesion: Most common homozygous tumor-suppressor deletion in bone tumor cell lines (15/36 EuroBoNeT lines) and frequent in primary OS and dedifferentiated/high-grade chondrosarcoma
key_markers: Loss of p16INK4a protein by IHC concordant with genomic deletion

defining_lesion: High baseline ploidy in OS; WGD emerges in a subset of PDX-derived cell lines relative to their parental PDX and patient tumor while expression profiles are largely maintained
key_markers: Genome-wide allelic imbalance, ploidy >2n by WGS/SNP array

defining_lesion: COSMIC signature 3 and large-scale-transition/LOH signatures reminiscent of BRCA deficiency in a large fraction of OS; basis of the S-HRD subtype and PARP-inhibitor rationale
key_markers: COSMIC SBS3, HRD score, BRCA2/TP53 deletions

defining_lesion: Recurrent somatic amplification/rearrangement of IGF pathway genes (IGF1R, IGF1, IGF2) in ~7-14% of OS; distinct patterns of genomic rearrangement defined by WGS
key_markers: IGF1R amplification, IGF1/IGF2 gain

defining_lesion: PI3K/mTOR alterations in ~24% of OS across TARGET-OS and orthogonal shRNA screens; common actionable vulnerability
key_markers: PIK3CA, PTEN, mTOR pathway alterations; p-mTOR by RPPA

defining_lesion: Biphasic small round cell + islands of hyaline cartilage; recurrent HEY1-NCOA2 fusion (in-frame HEY1 exon 4 to NCOA2 exon 13); rare IRF2BP2-CDX1
key_markers: HEY1-NCOA2 fusion by RT-PCR/FISH/RNA-seq; SOX9+, NKX3-1 not required; CD99 variable

defining_lesion: IDH1 or IDH2 hotspot mutations in ~50-60% of central chondrosarcomas and central/periosteal chondromas; absent in peripheral/secondary chondrosarcoma and other mesenchymal tumors; drives 2-HG and DNA hypermethylation
key_markers: IDH1 p.R132C/G/H/L/S; IDH2 p.R172S/W/G; D-2-hydroxyglutarate accumulation; CpG island hypermethylator phenotype

defining_lesion: Notochordal tumor of the axial skeleton (clivus, mobile spine, sacrum); brachyury (TBXT) is the lineage-defining and diagnostic marker and an essential dependency; germline TBXT duplication in familial chordoma; rs2305089 risk allele in sporadic disease
key_markers: Brachyury/TBXT nuclear IHC+, cytokeratin+, S100+, EMA+; frequent CDKN2A deletion; SMARCB1/INI1 loss in poorly differentiated chordoma

defining_lesion: Germline tandem duplication of the T/TBXT locus segregates with familial chordoma; T sequence variants characterized in familial and sporadic cases
key_markers: Germline TBXT copy gain

defining_lesion: Driver mutation in H3-3A (H3F3A) encoding histone H3.3 p.Gly34Trp (G34W) in >90% of GCTB, restricted to the mononuclear neoplastic stromal cells; rarer G34L/M/R/V
key_markers: H3.3 G34W mutation-specific antibody (clone RM263) IHC; RANKL-high stromal cells driving osteoclast-rich giant cells; denosumab target

subtype_name: H3F3A mutation diagnostic value in GCTB
defining_lesion: H3F3A G34 mutation distinguishes GCTB from osteoclast-rich mimics (ABC, chondroblastoma, non-ossifying fibroma, giant cell reparative granuloma)
key_markers: H3-3A G34W/L/M/R/V sequencing or IHC

defining_lesion: Driver mutation in H3-3B (H3F3B) encoding histone H3.3 p.Lys36Met (K36M) in ~95% of chondroblastomas; distinct from the H3F3A G34 mutations of GCTB; causes global H3K36me2/3 loss
key_markers: H3.3 K36M mutation-specific antibody IHC; S100+, SOX9+, DOG1+; epiphyseal location in skeletally immature patients

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
key_epigenetic_mechanism: SS18-SSX is incorporated into canonical BAF (cBAF) and ncBAF/GBAF complexes via SS18; the SSX C-terminus binds H2AK119ub-marked nucleosomes, causing eviction/proteasomal degradation of SMARCB1 (BAF47/INI1) and retargeting of the residual complex onto H3K27me3-marked polycomb domains and bivalent CpG-island promoters; opposition of PRC2 at these loci activates SOX2 and a broad neural/stem program. Retained SMARCB1 protein is markedly reduced (mosaic/reduced INI1 IHC). Creates a synthetic-lethal ncBAF (BRD9) dependency
key_markers: TLE1+, SS18-SSX fusion-specific antibody+, reduced/mosaic INI1, CD99 variable, EMA/CK focal, SOX2 up
pediatric_relevance: ~15-20% of non-RMS pediatric/AYA STS; the single most common non-RMS STS of adolescence; median age ~30 but a large pediatric tail

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Same BAF/ncBAF hijacking as SSX1; SSX2 fusions are enriched in monophasic tumors. SS18-SSX also hijacks KDM2B-PRC1.1 to non-methylated CpG islands, coupling variant PRC1 to BAF-driven activation
key_markers: As above
pediatric_relevance: As above

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: SS18::SSX4 or SS18L1(CREST)::SSX1; <1-2% of cases
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Presumed identical BAF-retargeting mechanism; too few cases for dedicated epigenomic study; no dedicated cell model exists
key_markers: As above
pediatric_relevance: Rare; case reports only in pediatric series

defining_lesion: Biallelic EED or SUZ12 loss (~70-90% of high-grade MPNST) on a background of NF1 +/- CDKN2A/B loss
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Complete loss of PRC2 catalytic output causes global erasure of H3K27me3; polycomb-repressed enhancers/promoters are de-repressed and gain H3K27ac and BRD4 occupancy; this amplifies RAS-MAPK target transcription and produces a distinctive globally H3K27me3-null methylome/chromatin state. Confers sensitivity to BET (BRD4) inhibition; H3K27me3 loss is a diagnostic IHC surrogate
key_markers: Loss of H3K27me3 (IHC), S100/SOX10 loss or patchy, loss of neurofibromin, CDKN2A/p16 loss, TRPS1 correlates with PRC2 loss
pediatric_relevance: Peak incidence 20-50y but 10-20% of MPNST arise in children/AYA with NF1; MPNST is the leading cause of NF1 mortality

defining_lesion: Germline NF1 + somatic NF1 second hit, arising in plexiform neurofibroma/ANNUBP
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Stepwise epigenomic progression: neurofibroma -> atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential (CDKN2A/B loss) -> MPNST (PRC2 loss, H3K27me3 erasure). Retained H3K27me3 in a subset defines a PRC2-intact group with distinct methylation class
key_markers: Neurofibromin loss, H3K27me3 loss (subset), CDKN2A/B deletion, SOX10 loss
pediatric_relevance: ~50% of MPNST are NF1-associated; NF1 patients have ~8-13% lifetime risk; pediatric onset common

defining_lesion: Somatic NF1/SUZ12/EED/CDKN2A alterations without NF1 syndrome
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Same PRC2-loss/H3K27me3-null epigenotype in the majority; radiation-associated cases show higher genomic complexity
key_markers: As above
pediatric_relevance: ~40% sporadic, ~10% post-radiation (relevant to survivors of childhood cancer)

WHO_2020_category: Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas of bone and soft tissue
defining_lesion: t(11;22)(p13;q12) EWSR1::WT1; EWSR1 exons 7-10 fused to WT1 exons 8-10; -KTS isoform is oncogenic
key_epigenetic_mechanism: The EWS low-complexity prion-like domain confers transactivation and condensate-forming capacity onto the WT1 zinc fingers, converting a repressor into a neomorphic activator. EWSR1-WT1 binds thousands of sites, most in distal enhancers, and creates de novo/neomorphic enhancers driving a hybrid mesenchymal-epithelial program and 'neogenes' (e.g. FGFRL1, LRRC15, CCND1, PDGFA, MSLN, ASCL1, ERBB/NTRK5 axis). Fusion-isoform (exon 7 vs 9 vs 10) dictates which enhancer set is engaged. Chromatin dependency on the fusion itself; lurbinectedin evicts EWS-WT1 from chromatin
key_markers: WT1 C-terminus+ (N-terminus-), desmin dot-like+, keratin+, EMA+, CD99 variable
pediatric_relevance: Classic AYA male tumor: median age 21-25y, M:F ~4:1, large pediatric fraction; abdominopelvic serosal

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: der(17)t(X;17)(p11;q25) unbalanced ASPSCR1(ASPL)::TFE3
key_epigenetic_mechanism: The ASPSCR1 UBX domain recruits hexameric VCP/p97 into the fusion transcription factor complex; ASPSCR1-TFE3 binds CLEAR/E-box elements and organises enhancer-promoter loops around VCP hexamers, generating a hyper-connected enhancer network that drives an angiogenic/lysosomal-autophagy MiT-family program (MET, ANGPTL2, PSAT1, lysosomal genes). Effectively a chromatin-looping neomorph rather than a simple TF gain
key_markers: TFE3 nuclear+ (IHC and FISH), PAS-diastase-resistant crystals, CD34- , desmin-/-, MyoD1-
pediatric_relevance: Median age 22-25y; ~20-25% under 20y; frequently presents with lung/brain metastases in adolescents

disease: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
key_epigenetic_mechanism: The EWS transactivation domain is fused to the bZIP DNA-binding domain of ATF1/CREB1, producing a constitutive, cAMP-independent activator that binds CRE elements in the MITF-M promoter. Ectopic MITF then acts as a lineage-survival master regulator, opening a melanocytic enhancer landscape (TYR, DCT, MLANA, GP100, BCL2, MET) in a mesenchymal cell of origin. Chimera also drives SOX10 and, via MITF, the same super-enhancer circuitry as melanoma - hence 'melanoma of soft parts'
key_markers: S100+, SOX10+, HMB45+, MelanA+, MITF+, BRAF/NRAS wild-type (distinguishes from melanoma)
pediatric_relevance: Peak 20-40y but a substantial adolescent fraction; distal extremities/tendons/aponeuroses; also gastrointestinal CCS-like (malignant GNET) with EWSR1::ATF1/CREB1

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: Biallelic SMARCB1 (INI1/BAF47) inactivation, usually 22q11 deletion, in a relatively quiet genome
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Loss of SMARCB1 destabilises cBAF; residual BAF is retained at super-enhancers but is lost from thousands of typical enhancers, which collapse and lose H3K27ac. PRC2/EZH2 then dominates at these loci, so the cell becomes dependent on EZH2 catalytic (and non-catalytic) activity - the mechanistic basis for tazemetostat approval. Bivalent promoters fail to be activated
key_markers: Loss of INI1/BAF47 (IHC), CK+, EMA+, CD34+ (~50%), ERG+ (subset)
pediatric_relevance: Distal type: adolescents and young adults, median 25-35y, hands/forearms; the paradigm SMARCB1-deficient sarcoma of AYA

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: SMARCB1 loss, more often by inactivating mutation; higher genomic complexity
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Same BAF-collapse/EZH2-dependency axis as distal type; more rhabdoid-like chromatin state approaching malignant rhabdoid tumor; DNA-methylation classifier separates proximal EpS from MRT
key_markers: INI1 loss, CK+, EMA+, rhabdoid morphology, CD34 less often+
pediatric_relevance: Pelvis/perineum/deep axial; older AYA, but documented in children (e.g. YCUS-5 from a 3-year-old)

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: Biallelic SMARCB1 inactivation (rarely SMARCA4); very low mutation burden
key_epigenetic_mechanism: SMARCB1 loss collapses cBAF occupancy at typical enhancers genome-wide while super-enhancers are retained; enhancers lose H3K27ac/H3K4me1 and de-differentiation programs (SOX2, MYC, cyclin D1) persist while lineage-specification enhancers and bivalent developmental promoters fail to activate. PRC2/EZH2 fills the vacated loci -> EZH2 dependency. Essentially a purely epigenetic cancer
key_markers: INI1/BAF47 loss (IHC), vimentin+, EMA+, CK+ variable; SMARCA4 loss in INI1-retained cases
pediatric_relevance: Infants and young children (median <2y); ~1/3 have germline SMARCB1 (rhabdoid tumor predisposition syndrome RTPS1; RTPS2 = SMARCA4)

WHO_2020_category: Kidney tumors (WHO Urinary and Male Genital, 5th ed.)
defining_lesion: Biallelic SMARCB1 loss
key_epigenetic_mechanism: As for extrarenal MRT; identical methylation class to extrarenal MRT and to ATRT-MYC in many classifiers
key_markers: INI1 loss, no WT1 expression (distinguishes from Wilms)
pediatric_relevance: Median age 11-18 months; ~2% of pediatric renal tumors; frequently synchronous with ATRT

defining_lesion: SMARCB1 loss, most often broad chr22q deletion
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Distinct DNA-methylation and enhancer landscape with high global methylation; melanosomal/tyrosinase program (TYR, MITF, DCT) driven by OTX2 and a melanocytic enhancer set; enriched for BMP pathway activity
key_markers: TYR+, MITF+, OTX2+, INI1 loss
pediatric_relevance: Infratentorial, youngest patients (median ~12 months); ~1/3 of ATRT

defining_lesion: SMARCB1 loss, more often focal/point mutation
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Intermediate global methylation; activation of SHH and NOTCH enhancer programs; high GLI2, MYCN, ASCL1, PTCH1; ASCL1 status further splits SHH-1/SHH-2
key_markers: MYCN+, GLI2+, ASCL1+, INI1 loss
pediatric_relevance: Supratentorial and infratentorial, median ~20 months; ~40% of ATRT

defining_lesion: SMARCB1 loss, often focal deletion
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Lowest global DNA methylation; MYC-driven enhancer landscape with HOX cluster activation (HOTAIR); epigenomically closest to extracranial/renal rhabdoid tumors
key_markers: MYC+, HOXC cluster+, INI1 loss
pediatric_relevance: Supratentorial, oldest ATRT patients (median ~2-3y), also occurs in older children/AYA

defining_lesion: Biallelic SMARCA4 (BRG1) loss with retained SMARCB1
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Loss of the BAF ATPase abolishes nucleosome remodelling at enhancers; similar enhancer collapse to SMARCB1 loss but no residual catalytic activity; associated with germline SMARCA4 (RTPS2) and with SCCOHT
key_markers: SMARCA4/BRG1 loss with retained INI1
pediatric_relevance: <5% of ATRT; very young infants; strong germline testing indication

WHO_2020_category: Fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumors (intermediate, rarely metastasising)
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Predominantly a kinase-signaling disease rather than a chromatin disease: the ETV6 SAM/PNT domain oligomerises NTRK3, giving ligand-independent TRKC activation -> MAPK/PI3K. Downstream epigenetic consequence is a distinct, tightly clustered DNA-methylation class (shared with cellular/congenital mesoblastic nephroma) used diagnostically; no primary chromatin-modifier lesion
key_markers: Pan-TRK+ (nuclear/cytoplasmic), S100 variable, CD34 patchy, SMA variable
pediatric_relevance: Classic tumor of infants <1-2y; >90% cured with TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib/entrectinib); near-identical to cellular congenital mesoblastic nephroma

WHO_2020_category: Fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumors (emerging entity: NTRK-rearranged spindle cell neoplasm)
defining_lesion: LMNA::NTRK1 and other NTRK1/NTRK2 fusions
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Same kinase-oligomerisation logic; these tumors form their own methylation class distinct from ETV6::NTRK3 IFS, with S100/CD34 co-expression and a lipofibromatosis-like histology
key_markers: Pan-TRK+, S100+ and CD34+ co-expression
pediatric_relevance: Infants through adolescents; TRK-inhibitor responsive

defining_lesion: SND1::BRAF, EML4::NTRK3, RBPMS::MET, and BRAF/RAF1 kinase fusions in NTRK-negative IFS-like tumors
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Kinase-fusion driven MAPK activation without a primary epigenetic lesion; methylation profiling separates these from ETV6::NTRK3 IFS
key_markers: Pan-TRK-negative, BRAF/RAF1 fusion by RNA sequencing
pediatric_relevance: Infants; important because they are TRK-inhibitor refractory but MEK/RAF-inhibitor sensitive

WHO_2020_category: Fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumors (intermediate, rarely metastasising)
defining_lesion: ALK fusions in ~50-70%; RANBP2::ALK and RRBP1::ALK define epithelioid inflammatory myofibroblastic sarcoma
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Kinase-fusion driven; the fusion partner dictates ALK subcellular localisation (nuclear-membranous for RANBP2) and thereby which transcriptional programs are engaged. No characterized primary chromatin lesion; epigenomic literature is essentially absent - a genuine gap
key_markers: ALK+ (IHC pattern informative: cytoplasmic vs nuclear-membranous), SMA+, desmin variable, ROS1/NTRK3 in ALK-negative cases
pediatric_relevance: Classic tumor of children and AYA (lung, abdomen, bladder); crizotinib/lorlatinib responsive

defining_lesion: TFG::ROS1, YWHAE::ROS1, ETV6::NTRK3, NAB2::PDGFRB
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Kinase-fusion driven; no defined chromatin mechanism
key_markers: ROS1+, pan-TRK+ depending on fusion
pediatric_relevance: ALK-negative pediatric IMT; entrectinib/crizotinib responsive

defining_lesion: t(1;3)(p36;q25) WWTR1::CAMTA1 in >90%
key_epigenetic_mechanism: TAZ-CAMTA1 is constitutively nuclear (escapes LATS/14-3-3 cytoplasmic sequestration) and retains the TAZ TEAD-binding domain; it therefore hijacks TEAD1-4 at YAP/TAZ enhancers and, via the CAMTA1 moiety, recruits the ATAC histone-acetyltransferase complex, converting a Hippo-restrained program into a constitutive one. Reprograms endothelial cells directly; TEAD-palmitoylation inhibitors and the TAZ-CAMTA1-TEAD interface are the tractable targets
key_markers: CAMTA1 nuclear+ (IHC), ERG+, CD31+, CD34+, TFE3- , keratin+ in a subset
pediatric_relevance: Rare but well described in children and AYA; multifocal hepatic/pulmonary/bone disease; indolent-to-aggressive

defining_lesion: YAP1::TFE3 in ~5-10%; younger patients, vasoformative morphology
key_epigenetic_mechanism: YAP1 TEAD-binding domain fused to the TFE3 DNA-binding/leucine-zipper domain; drives a hybrid YAP-TEAD/MiT-family transcriptional output at CLEAR and TEAD elements
key_markers: TFE3 nuclear+, CAMTA1-, ERG+, CD31+
pediatric_relevance: Enriched in young adults and adolescents

WHO_2020_category: Vascular tumors of soft tissue (intermediate, rarely metastasising)
defining_lesion: t(7;19)(q22;q13) SERPINE1::FOSB
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Promoter-swap enhancer hijacking: the strong constitutive SERPINE1 (or ACTB) promoter/enhancer is placed upstream of FOSB, causing massive FOSB overexpression and constitutive AP-1 transcription factor activity that remodels the endothelial enhancer landscape
key_markers: FOSB nuclear+ (IHC), CD31+, ERG+, keratin AE1/AE3+, CD34-
pediatric_relevance: Predominantly adolescents and young adult males; multifocal in one limb, bone and soft tissue

subtype_name: Pediatric/AYA angiosarcoma (primary, secondary, radiation- and lymphoedema-associated)
defining_lesion: MYC amplification (8q24) in radiation/lymphoedema-associated; KDR, PTPRB, PLCG1, TP53 in primary; no single defining lesion
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Heterogeneous. Radiation-associated angiosarcoma shows high-level MYC amplification with FLT4 co-amplification and reduced H3K27me3 by IHC. Primary angiosarcoma shows recurrent chromatin-modifier mutations (ARID1A, KDM6A, KMT2D) and, in a subset, an endothelial super-enhancer program driven by SOX18/ERG/FLI1. Head-and-neck cutaneous cases have a UV signature
key_markers: CD31+, ERG+, FLI1+, MYC+ (amplified cases), reduced H3K27me3 in radiation-associated
pediatric_relevance: Rare in children but a documented late effect in survivors of childhood cancer treated with radiation (secondary angiosarcoma)

key_epigenetic_mechanism: The FET low-complexity prion-like domain drives liquid-liquid phase separation, so FUS-DDIT3 forms nuclear condensates that concentrate transcriptional machinery on DDIT3/C-EBP-family target elements. The fusion acts as a dominant-negative on C/EBP-beta while neomorphically activating targets (IL6, NF-kB via NFKBIZ, PPARG blockade), locking cells in an adipocytic differentiation arrest. Trabectedin works by evicting FUS-DDIT3 from chromatin and restoring adipocytic differentiation
key_markers: DDIT3(CHOP) nuclear+, NY-ESO-1 strongly+ (immunotherapy target), S100 variable, MDM2/CDK4 not amplified
pediatric_relevance: Rare <10y but the most common liposarcoma of adolescents/young adults; median ~35y with a definite AYA tail; distinct pattern of extrapulmonary metastasis

subtype_name: COL1A1::PDGFB (incl. giant-cell fibroblastoma and Bednar/pigmented variants)
WHO_2020_category: Fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumors (intermediate, locally aggressive)
defining_lesion: Supernumerary ring chromosome r(17;22) or t(17;22) generating COL1A1::PDGFB
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Classic enhancer/promoter hijacking: PDGFB is placed under the powerful, constitutively active COL1A1 promoter, producing an autocrine PDGFB-PDGFRB loop. No primary chromatin-modifier lesion; DNA methylation profiling nevertheless separates DFSP from other fibroblastic tumors. Fibrosarcomatous transformation adds CDKN2A/TERT changes
key_markers: CD34 diffusely+, factor XIIIa-, S100-, PDGFB fusion by FISH/RNAseq
pediatric_relevance: Congenital and pediatric DFSP well described (giant-cell fibroblastoma is the pediatric variant); imatinib-responsive

WHO_2020_category: Fibroblastic and myofibroblastic tumors (intermediate, locally aggressive)
defining_lesion: CTNNB1 exon 3 hotspots T41A, S45F, S45P (~85%) or germline APC (FAP, ~10-15%)
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Stabilised beta-catenin enters the nucleus and partners TCF/LEF at WNT-responsive enhancers, recruiting CBP/p300 and BRD4; the resulting super-enhancer output (AXIN2, MYC, CCND1) is the disease driver. Gamma-secretase inhibition (nirogacestat) works through NOTCH crosstalk with this program. No primary chromatin-modifier lesion
key_markers: Nuclear beta-catenin+, SMA variable, CD34- , desmin-
pediatric_relevance: Bimodal: infantile/pediatric desmoids and an AYA peak; FAP association mandates colonoscopy in children

subtype_name: SDH-deficient GIST (pediatric/'wild-type' GIST, Carney triad, Carney-Stratakis)
WHO_2020_category: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (WHO Digestive System, 5th ed.)
defining_lesion: SDHA/B/C/D germline or somatic loss-of-function, OR epigenetic SDHC promoter hypermethylation (SDHC epimutation, Carney triad); KIT/PDGFRA wild-type
key_epigenetic_mechanism: The flagship epigenetic sarcoma. Loss of SDH causes succinate accumulation, which competitively inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases (TET1/2/3 and the KDM family). The result is a global, CpG-island-dominant DNA hypermethylation phenotype far exceeding KIT-mutant GIST. Hypermethylation of CTCF binding sites disrupts insulated neighbourhood boundaries, allowing an FGF3/FGF4 locus enhancer to escape its TAD and aberrantly activate FGF4 - enhancer hijacking by topology loss. Also drives pseudohypoxia (HIF stabilisation) and IGF1R overexpression. SDHC epimutation itself is a primary epigenetic lesion with no coding mutation
key_markers: Loss of SDHB (IHC) in all SDH-deficient GIST; loss of SDHA additionally in SDHA-mutant cases; DOG1+, KIT+, multinodular/plexiform gastric architecture, lymph node metastases
pediatric_relevance: Essentially the entire pediatric GIST population: >85% of GIST in children and adolescents is SDH-deficient, female predominant, gastric, indolent but node-metastasising, and imatinib-refractory. This is the entity where an epigenomic white paper matters most and where models are almost absent

defining_lesion: KIT exon 11/9 or PDGFRA exon 18 (D842V) activating mutations
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Kinase-driven; a globally hypomethylated genome relative to SDH-deficient GIST. ETV1 acts as a lineage-survival master transcription factor whose enhancer network is stabilised by KIT signaling - a signaling-to-enhancer feedback loop rather than a primary chromatin lesion
key_markers: KIT(CD117)+, DOG1+, SDHB retained
pediatric_relevance: Rare in children (<15% of pediatric GIST); mostly a NF1- or syndromic context when it occurs

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
key_epigenetic_mechanism: FET-domain transactivation grafted onto the NR4A3 orphan nuclear receptor: the chimera binds NBRE/NurRE elements and neomorphically activates a neuroendocrine/axon-guidance program (the partner gene determines which - TAF15 fusions give a rhabdoid phenotype and different axon-guidance output). NR4A3 also derepresses via SIX/HOX loci. Distinctive DNA-methylation class
key_markers: NR4A3 rearrangement by FISH/RNAseq, S100 usually negative, INSM1/synaptophysin variable, EMA/CK-
pediatric_relevance: Predominantly 5th-6th decade; distinctly uncommon in children - include for completeness and because H-EMC-SS is widely (mis)used

defining_lesion: t(7;16)(q33;p11) FUS::CREB3L2 (~90%); FUS::CREB3L1 or EWSR1::CREB3L1 in a minority
key_epigenetic_mechanism: FET low-complexity domain fused to the bZIP CREB3L2 transcription factor, which normally requires regulated intramembrane proteolysis for activation; the fusion is constitutively nuclear and active, driving a secretory/ER-stress program with massive MUC4 induction. Aberrant phase separation and membranous organelle remodelling have been implicated
key_markers: MUC4 diffusely+ (highly sensitive/specific), EMA focal+, S100- , SMA-
pediatric_relevance: Well documented in children and AYA (median ~34y, but pediatric cases common); deceptively bland histology with very late metastasis

defining_lesion: EWSR1::CREB3L1 (~70% of pure SEF); hybrid LGFMS-SEF carries FUS::CREB3L2
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Same FET-bZIP mechanism as LGFMS with a shift in output toward a collagenous/sclerosing program; SEF and LGFMS are epigenomically related but separable by methylation class; SEF is far more aggressive
key_markers: MUC4+ (in hybrid and many pure SEF), EMA+, keratin-
pediatric_relevance: Rare in children; more aggressive than LGFMS with high metastatic rate

subtype_name: TSC1/TSC2-altered PEComa (incl. angiomyolipoma, LAM, clear cell 'sugar' tumor)
WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation (PEComatous tumors)
defining_lesion: Biallelic TSC1 or TSC2 loss; germline in tuberous sclerosis complex
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Constitutive mTORC1 activation. The epigenetic consequence is indirect but real: mTORC1 drives MITF/TFE3/TFEB nuclear retention (via RagGTPase-dependent phosphorylation) and thereby a CLEAR-network lysosomal/autophagy enhancer program, plus a metabolic reprogramming that alters acetyl-CoA availability for histone acetylation. Sirolimus/nab-sirolimus responsive
key_markers: HMB45+, MelanA+, cathepsin K+, SMA+, TFE3 usually negative, loss of TSC2/tuberin
pediatric_relevance: Angiomyolipoma and LAM in tuberous sclerosis present in children/adolescents; malignant PEComa is rare in children

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: TFE3 (Xp11.2) rearrangement; mutually exclusive with TSC alterations
key_epigenetic_mechanism: MiT/TFE family fusion drives a constitutive CLEAR-element lysosomal/autophagy enhancer program independent of mTORC1; mechanistically parallel to ASPS (ASPSCR1::TFE3) and Xp11 translocation RCC, and these three form overlapping methylation neighbourhoods. Recently shown to induce stem-like transcriptional programs distinct from TSC-altered PEComa
key_markers: TFE3 strong nuclear+, HMB45+, cathepsin K+, SMA often negative, melanocytic markers variable
pediatric_relevance: Enriched in young patients including adolescents; poorer response to mTOR inhibitors than TSC-altered PEComa

subtype_name: UPS / undifferentiated sarcoma NOS (incl. undifferentiated round cell/spindle cell/epithelioid)
defining_lesion: No defining lesion; complex karyotype, chromothripsis, TP53/RB1/ATRX loss, high copy-number burden
key_epigenetic_mechanism: No single driver; a genomically chaotic group. Epigenomically defined by exclusion - methylation classifiers place true UPS in a broad, low-confidence cluster, and a substantial fraction of tumors historically called pediatric UPS are reclassified by methylation into defined entities (MPNST, rhabdomyosarcoma, CIC- or BCOR-altered sarcoma, inflammatory rhabdomyoblastic tumor). Recurrent chromatin-modifier hits (ATRX, KMT2D, ARID1A) and ALT are common
key_markers: Diagnosis of exclusion: desmin-, S100-, CD34-, INI1 retained, myogenin-
pediatric_relevance: 'Undifferentiated sarcoma' is a large bucket in COG/pediatric trials; methylation profiling is the single highest-yield reclassification tool in this group

subtype_name: Conventional LMS (soft tissue, uterine, bone, vascular)
defining_lesion: No defining fusion; recurrent TP53, RB1, PTEN, ATRX loss; frequent whole-genome doubling
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Complex-genome sarcoma. Two epigenetic themes: (i) ATRX loss (~25-30%) drives alternative lengthening of telomeres and pericentromeric/telomeric heterochromatin destabilisation; (ii) methylation profiling separates conventional LMS from uterine LMS and from an 'undifferentiated' methylation group, and identifies a distinct inflamed/immune subtype. EZH2 overexpression and MYOCD/SRF enhancer programs define the smooth-muscle lineage output
key_markers: SMA+, desmin+, h-caldesmon+, ATRX loss (subset), TP53 aberrant
pediatric_relevance: Uncommon in children; EBV-associated smooth muscle tumor is the pediatric-relevant mimic (immunosuppressed/HIV/post-transplant); inherited LMS in Li-Fraumeni and RB1-survivor cohorts

WHO_2020_category: Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas of bone and soft tissue
key_epigenetic_mechanism: The DUX4 C-terminus supplies a p300-recruiting transactivation domain to the CIC repressor, converting it into a potent activator at CIC-binding octamer motifs; this creates de novo active enhancers at ETV1/ETV4/ETV5 and a PEA3 program. Distinct methylation class, clearly separable from Ewing sarcoma
key_markers: WT1+, ETV4+, DUX4 C-terminus+, CD99 patchy (unlike Ewing), NKX2-2-
pediatric_relevance: Adolescents and young adults; more aggressive and chemo-resistant than Ewing; explicitly non-Ewing

subtype_name: BCOR::CCNB3, BCOR internal tandem duplication (ITD), YWHAE::NUTM2B
WHO_2020_category: Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas of bone and soft tissue
defining_lesion: X-chromosome paracentric inversion BCOR::CCNB3 (adolescent males); BCOR-ITD in infantile undifferentiated round cell sarcoma / primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumor of infancy
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Directly a polycomb disease: BCOR is a core component of the non-canonical PRC1.1 complex. BCOR::CCNB3 and BCOR-ITD both disrupt the BCOR PUFD-PCGF1 interface, redistributing PRC1.1 and altering H2AK119ub deposition; the result is derepression of a HOX/SATB2/BCOR-high program. Forms a tight, distinctive DNA-methylation class
key_markers: BCOR+ (IHC), CCNB3+ (in BCOR::CCNB3), SATB2+, TLE1+, cyclin D1+, CD99 variable
pediatric_relevance: BCOR::CCNB3 is characteristically an adolescent male bone tumor; BCOR-ITD tumors occur in infants (<1y). Both are important non-Ewing round cell sarcomas of childhood

defining_lesion: Intrachromosomal 12q13 inversion NAB2::STAT6
key_epigenetic_mechanism: NAB2 is a transcriptional repressor of EGR1; fusion to the STAT6 transactivation domain converts it into a constitutive EGR1-target activator, engaging EGR1-responsive enhancers (IGF2, FGF2, ALDH1). Fusion variant (NAB2ex4-STAT6ex2/3 vs ex6-ex16/17) correlates with age, site and aggressiveness
key_markers: STAT6 nuclear+ (IHC), CD34+, ALDH1+, GRIA2+
pediatric_relevance: Uncommon but documented in children; NAB2ex4-STAT6ex2/3 variant occurs in younger patients

disease: Myoepithelial tumor / myoepithelial carcinoma of soft tissue
WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: EWSR1 (or FUS) rearrangement in ~45%; PLAG1 fusions enriched in pediatric cases; SMARCB1 loss in ~10-40% of pediatric myoepithelial carcinoma
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Two coexisting mechanisms: (i) FET-fusion neomorphic transactivation of developmental transcription factors (POU5F1/OCT4, PBX1); (ii) in a substantial pediatric subset, SMARCB1 loss with the same BAF-collapse/EZH2-dependency biology as rhabdoid tumor and epithelioid sarcoma
key_markers: S100+/SOX10+, keratin+, EMA+, GFAP variable, INI1 loss in a subset
pediatric_relevance: EWSR1::POU5F1 tumors are enriched in children; SMARCB1-deficient pediatric myoepithelial carcinoma behaves like a rhabdoid tumor

WHO_2020_category: Soft tissue: tumors of uncertain differentiation
defining_lesion: PHF1 (6p21) rearrangement in ~60-85%; partners are NuA4/TIP60 complex components
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Direct chromatin-complex fusion: PHF1 is a PRC2-associated Tudor-domain reader (PCL1) and its partners EP400/MEAF6/EPC1 are NuA4/TIP60 histone acetyltransferase subunits. The fusion physically bridges an H3K36me3-reading polycomb accessory factor to a HAT complex, mistargeting acetylation to polycomb domains - a polycomb/HAT chimera
key_markers: S100+ (~70%), desmin variable, INI1 retained, PHF1 rearrangement by FISH
pediatric_relevance: Wide age range including children and adolescents; malignant OFMT is rare

defining_lesion: t(1;2)(p13;q37) CSF1::COL6A3 and other CSF1 rearrangements
key_epigenetic_mechanism: Promoter/enhancer hijacking: CSF1 is placed under the COL6A3 promoter, producing a landscape effect in which a small population of neoplastic cells recruits a massive CSF1R-positive non-neoplastic macrophage infiltrate. The tumor bulk is therefore driven by a paracrine, not cell-autonomous, program; pexidartinib targets CSF1R
key_markers: CSF1 by ISH/FISH, clusterin+, desmin+ dendritic cells, CD68+ macrophage background
pediatric_relevance: Diffuse-type TGCT occurs in adolescents and young adults (knee, hip); locally destructive
